\section*{Hypothesis Testing}
\subsection*{Key Concepts}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \csheetbold{Null hypothesis} ($H_0$): status quo, assumed true until evidence suggests otherwise
  \item \csheetbold{Alternative hypothesis} ($H_1$ or $H_a$): contradicts $H_0$, what we seek evidence for
  \item \csheetbold{Test statistic}: computed from sample data, used to decide between $H_0$ and $H_1$
  \item \csheetbold{p-value}: probability of observing data as extreme as the sample, assuming $H_0$ is true
  \item \csheetbold{Significance level} $\alpha$: threshold for rejecting $H_0$ (commonly 0.05, 0.01)
\end{itemize}
\subsection*{Common Tests}
\begin{csheettable}{llll}
\tblheader{Test} & \tblheader{Purpose} & \tblheader{Test Statistic} & \tblheader{Assumptions} \\
\midrule
z-test & Compare sample mean vs population mean & $z = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu}{\sigma / \sqrt{n}}$ & Known $\sigma$, normal population or large $n$ \\
t-test & Compare means, unknown $\sigma$ & $t = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu}{s / \sqrt{n}}$ & Normal population, unknown $\sigma$ \\
Paired t-test & Compare paired measurements & $t = \frac{\bar{d}}{s_d / \sqrt{n}}$ & Differences are normal \\
Two-sample t-test & Compare two independent means & $t = \frac{\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2}{s_p \sqrt{\frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_2}}}$ & Equal variances, normal populations \\
Chi-square test & Test association / goodness-of-fit & $\chi^2 = \sum \frac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}$ & Expected counts $\ge 5$ \\
F-test & Compare two variances & $F = \frac{s_1^2}{s_2^2}$ & Normal populations \\
\end{csheettable}
\subsection*{Decision Rule}
Two approaches:\par
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \csheetbold{p-value approach}: reject $H_0$ if $\text{p-value} < \alpha$
  \item \csheetbold{Critical value approach}: reject $H_0$ if $|\text{test statistic}| > \text{critical value}$
\end{enumerate}
\subsection*{Type I and Type II Errors}
\begin{csheettable}{p{0.28\columnwidth}p{0.28\columnwidth}p{0.38\columnwidth}}
\tblheader{} & \tblheader{$H_0$ true} & \tblheader{$H_0$ false} \\
\midrule
\csheetbold{Reject $H_0$} & Type I error ($\alpha$) & Correct \\
\csheetbold{Fail to reject $H_0$} & Correct & Type II error ($\beta$) \\
\end{csheettable}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \csheetbold{Power}: $1 - \beta$, probability of correctly rejecting a false $H_0$
\end{itemize}
\subsection*{Confidence Interval vs Hypothesis Test}
Confidence interval contains \csheetbold{all plausible values} of the parameter.\par
\begin{csheetcode}
If 95% CI contains the null value   → do not reject H₀ at α = 0.05
If 95% CI excludes the null value   → reject H₀ at α = 0.05
\end{csheetcode}
\csheetrule
\section*{ANOVA (Analysis of Variance)}
\subsection*{One-Way ANOVA}
Compare means of $k \ge 3$ groups.\par
\$\$\par
F = \frac{\text{between-group variability}}{\text{within-group variability}} = \frac{SSB/(k-1)}{SSW/(n-k)}\par
\$\$\par
\csheetbold{Assumptions}: independence, normality, equal variance across groups.\par
\subsection*{Two-Way ANOVA}
Factors: A (rows), B (columns), interaction A$\times$B.\par
\begin{csheettable}{lllll}
\tblheader{Source} & \tblheader{df} & \tblheader{SS} & \tblheader{MS} & \tblheader{F} \\
\midrule
Factor A & $a-1$ & SSA & MSA = SSA/(a-1) & MSA/MSE \\
Factor B & $b-1$ & SSB & MSB = SSB/(b-1) & MSB/MSE \\
Interaction & $(a-1)(b-1)$ & SSAB & MSAB = SSAB/(df) & MSAB/MSE \\
Error & $n-ab$ & SSE & MSE = SSE/(n-ab) &  \\
Total & $n-1$ & SST &  &  \\
\end{csheettable}
\subsection*{Post-hoc Tests}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \csheetbold{Tukey's HSD}: compare all pairwise means, controls family-wise error rate
  \item \csheetbold{Bonferroni correction}: adjust $\alpha$ by dividing by number of comparisons
\end{itemize}
\csheetrule
\section*{Regression}
\subsection*{Simple Linear Regression}
\$\$\par
y\_i = \beta\_0 + \beta\_1 x\_i + \varepsilon\_i, \quad \varepsilon\_i \sim N(0, \sigma\textasciicircum{}2)\par
\$\$\par
\csheetbold{Estimates}:\par
\$\$\par
\hat{\beta}\_1 = \frac{\sum (x\_i - \bar{x})(y\_i - \bar{y})}{\sum (x\_i - \bar{x})\textasciicircum{}2}, \quad\par
\hat{\beta}\_0 = \bar{y} - \hat{\beta}\_1 \bar{x}\par
\$\$\par
\subsection*{R-squared (Coefficient of Determination)}
\$\$\par
R\textasciicircum{}2 = 1 - \frac{SSE}{SST} = \frac{SSR}{SST}\par
\$\$\par
Interpreted as "proportion of variance in $y$ explained by $x$."\par
\subsection*{ANOVA Table for Regression}
\begin{csheettable}{lllll}
\tblheader{Source} & \tblheader{df} & \tblheader{SS} & \tblheader{MS} & \tblheader{F} \\
\midrule
Regression & 1 & SSR & MSR = SSR/1 & MSR/MSE \\
Residual & $n-2$ & SSE & MSE = SSE/(n-2) &  \\
Total & $n-1$ & SST &  &  \\
\end{csheettable}
\subsection*{Model Diagnostics}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \csheetbold{Residuals vs. fitted}: check constant variance
  \item \csheetbold{Q-Q plot}: check normality
  \item \csheetbold{Cook's distance}: identify influential points
\end{itemize}
\begin{csheetcode}
Rule of thumb: D_i > 4/n is influential
\end{csheetcode}
\csheetrule
\section*{Distribution Relationships}
\begin{csheetcode}
Normal(μ, σ²) ────→ t(df)          [when σ unknown, estimated by s]
Normal(0, 1)   ────→ χ²(k)         [sum of k squared z-scores]
t(k)           ────→ F(1, k)       [square of t-statistic]
χ²(k₁)/k₁
──────────    ═════   F(k₁, k₂)   [ratio of two chi-squares]
χ²(k₂)/k₂
\end{csheetcode}
